chronology: Defined after prior integrated values were known, before calculating these new cost-recovery scenarios. This is not valuation-blind research.
base: Root selected quarterly delivery, revised Other DCAI, component margins and normalized CPU growth.
scope: Host Foundry cost recovery fails or arrives later despite unchanged selected CPU/client deliveries. This is a distinct cost/process/depreciation outcome, not another penalty for the same missing revenue.

flat_2027_loss.reason: No nominal reduction of the selected 2027 loss through 2040. Terminal loss grows 3% consistently with the model's perpetual scale convention. This is a persistent cost failure, not a probability-weighted forecast.

two_year_recovery_delay.after2032: Hold 2.5B divided by actual selected 2032 Products revenue, scaling profit with actual Products sales thereafter.
two_year_recovery_delay.reason: The original 2028/2029/2030 dollar recovery milestones occur in 2030/2031/2032. No immediate catch-up to the original normalized profit level is assumed.

breakeven_without_mature_profit.reason: A meaningful recovery reaches breakeven by 2030, but host manufacturing contributes no positive mature profit. Packaging overlay remains separately unchanged.

held_fixed: All CPU, client, Other DCAI and external revenue paths
DCAI, CCPG, corporate and net incremental packaging profit
Physical capital budgets, depreciation, working capital, leases and minority claims
Finite tax credits and financing assumptions; recalculate ordinary operating tax only through existing engine
accounting: Replace the host Foundry profit line; change group EBIT by exactly the difference. Do not add a separate 50% revenue response or factory-absorption penalty. Holding booked Products margins fixed assumes the cost miss remains at Foundry under unchanged transfer conventions; the consolidated delta is what matters.
limitations: Constant deliveries with different cash operating costs can occur through yields, input costs, ramp expenses or process R&D. With D&A held fixed, this stress does not represent an additional noncash depreciation or impairment charge: such a charge would require its corresponding cash-flow addback. The scenario does not identify the cost mechanism or refund committed investment. Any financing-floor breach is flagged rather than silently funded.
